253gaojigongfa.title: Advanced Practices After Opening the Governing Vessel
253gaojigongfa.author: Li Shaobo
253gaojigongfa.excerpt: Most people who study the True Qi Circulation Method on their own, upon reaching the stage of "opening the Governing Vessel," believe they have completed all five steps of the practice. In fact they have completed only the first four steps of its elementary stage, and very few ever grasp the fifth step. Even when someone enters stillness well, the advanced states that arise in that stillness instead

254zhoutiangong.title: The Heavenly Circuit Practice
254zhoutiangong.author: Mingde
254zhoutiangong.excerpt: The Heavenly Circuit practice makes the true qi circulate through the body in a heavenly circuit, thereby moving the qi, invigorating the blood, dissolving stagnation and stasis, returning the essence to nourish the brain, and thus warding off illness, strengthening immunity, and prolonging life.

255haorenge.title: Song of the Good Man (Annotated)
255haorenge.author: Lü Xinwu
255haorenge.excerpt: Editor's note: The Master (Lü Xinwu) was named Kun, style name Shujian, a native of Ningling, a jinshi of the Jiajing reign of the Ming dynasty, who rose to the office of Junior Minister of Justice.

256chengxinxingshan.title: Practicing Good with a Sincere Heart
256chengxinxingshan.excerpt: Translation: The coming of misfortune and blessing has no other cause than what one’s own thoughts and actions summon forth. The retribution of good and evil from one’s thoughts and actions is like a shadow following the body and moving in accord with it—do evil and misfortune comes; do good and blessing comes.

257nizhuanshuailao.title: Reversing Aging by Refining the Jiaji Gates
257nizhuanshuailao.excerpt: Always keep this mind, retreating it into the Jiaji aperture, guarding it without ever letting it depart.

258quanzhenqizizhuan.title: Biography of the Seven Perfected Ones
258quanzhenqizizhuan.excerpt: In all the world no task is hard to do; / the fear is but a heart resolved and true.

259jingzongrumen.title: Entering the Pure Land School
259jingzongrumen.author: Zhanran
259jingzongrumen.excerpt: The purpose of studying Buddhism is to become a Buddha and deliver sentient beings. For an ordinary being to cultivate and attain Buddhahood there are two great stages: first, to escape the cycle of rebirth; second, to fully realize Buddhahood. The goal of the Buddhist practitioner in this life is to escape the cycle of the six realms of rebirth.

260jinianjiguan.title: Observing the Mind While Reciting the Buddha's Name
260jinianjiguan.author: Zhanran
260jinianjiguan.excerpt: Observing-the-mind recitation means that while reciting the Buddha's name, one contemplates the present single thought (reciting and contemplating at once). It is a most incisive and wondrous method, able to achieve steadily: the moment the Buddha's name is raised, all deluded thoughts vanish.

261lengqiejing.title: Lankavatara Sutra
261lengqiejing.excerpt: Preface to the Lankavatara Sutra, by Jiang Zhiqi, Attendant Counsellor and Auxiliary Director of Transport, and the second preface written out by Su Shi; followed by Fascicle One of the Sutra of the Precious Lankavatara, the All Buddha-Words Mind Chapter, Part One of One, opening with Mahamati's praise of the Buddha and his hundred and eight questions.

264gongtongyifashen.author: Zhanran

268zenyangkandaiyezhang.author: Venerable Master Mengcan
268zenyangkandaiyezhang.excerpt: True blessings and wisdom will then manifest before you.

269yigenianforendezishu.title: Dual Cultivation of Nature and Life
269yigenianforendezishu.author: The Essentials of Breathing Buddha-Recitation
269yigenianforendezishu.excerpt: [Dual cultivation of nature and life] Cultivation of nature: liberation of one's own nature (escaping the six realms of samsara); cultivation of life: health and longevity.

272nianfojingju.title: Admonitory Sayings on Buddha-Recitation (Four Passages)
272nianfojingju.excerpt: Those who practice the Pure Land must plainly oppose birth and death — this is not a matter to merely speak of and then let rest. You must reflect that impermanence is swift and time waits for no one, and make this one single task of your life. If you advance halfway and retreat halfway, half believing and half doubting, then when it comes (when it comes to the moment of death), what use will it be? How can you escape the cycle of rebirth?

273wumingmeng.title: The Dream of Ignorance
273wumingmeng.author: Zhanran
273wumingmeng.excerpt: Q: Why is it said that “all dharmas are illusions”?

274baizhangyehu.title: Baizhang's Wild Fox
274baizhangyehu.author: Annotated by Zhiyu
274baizhangyehu.excerpt: Whenever the Master (Master Baizhang) ascended the hall, an old man followed the assembly to hear the Dharma. One day, when the assembly withdrew, only the old man remained. The Master asked: “Who are you?” The old man said: “I am not a human being. In the time of the past Buddha Kashyapa, I once dwelt on this mountain. A student asked me: ‘Does a great practitioner still fall into cause and effect or not (does a great practitioner still receive or not receive karmic retribution)?’”

275zhengdaogezhu.title: Notes on the Song of Enlightenment
275zhengdaogezhu.author: Zhanran (annotator)
275zhengdaogezhu.excerpt: The Song of Enlightenment describes the dream of ignorance awakened — the realm in which, for example, the song says, "the dharmakāya awakened — not a single thing is there," "in the dream the six destinies are plainly there; once awakened, the great thousand worlds are empty and bare," and so on. The Song of Enlightenment shares with the Diamond Sutra, the Heart Sutra, and the Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch the same core: it teaches the realization and entry into the patience of the unborn, causing the self-nature to return to its original source.

276sanshixinian.title: Three Sessions of Mind-Recollection by Master Zhongfeng, Annotated
276sanshixinian.author: Annotated by Zhanran
276sanshixinian.excerpt: Note: The heading of each discourse has been added for convenient reading; it is not part of the original text.

277linianyizhuo.author: Annotated by Zhanran
277linianyizhuo.excerpt: (From the Dream Journey Collection: Instruction for the Chan Practitioner Liaoxin Hai)

278-1jianxingshixing.title: The Seeing-Nature Is the Mind
278-1jianxingshixing.author: Mingde
278-1jianxingshixing.excerpt: [Ānanda, you answered me earlier that you see my radiant fist. Where does this fist’s radiance come from? How does it become a fist? With what do you see it? Ānanda said: Because the Buddha’s whole body is like Jambu-river gold, glowing (xì) like a jeweled mountain, born of purity, it has radiance. I actually saw with my eyes the five wheel-fingered tips bend and clench to show people, and so there is the appearance of a fist.]

278-2jianxingbudong.title: The Seeing-Nature Is Unmoving
278-2jianxingbudong.author: Annotated by Mingde
278-2jianxingbudong.excerpt: At that time the World-Honored One stretched forth his hand — soft as cotton, adorned with the marks of the net and of the wheel, and radiant — opened his five fingers, and instructed and admonished Ananda and the great assembly: "When I first attained the Way, in the Deer Garden, I said to Kaundinya and the five monks and to the four assemblies of you: 'All beings fail to attain bodhi and arhatship because they are misled by the defilements of guest-dust.' At that time, because of what did you awaken, that you have now attained the holy fruit?

278-3jianxingbumie.title: The Seeing-Nature Does Not Perish
278-3jianxingbumie.author: Annotated by Mingde
278-3jianxingbumie.excerpt: At that time King Prasenajit rose and addressed the Buddha: “In the past, before I received the admonitions of the Buddhas, I saw Katyayana and Vairatiputra, who all said that this body is annihilated after death, and called this nirvana. Although I have now met the Buddha, I still harbor doubt. How may this mind be revealed and realized to dwell in the ground of neither arising nor ceasing? Now the whole assembly, all those with outflows, all wish to hear.”

279wajietongkuzhishen.title: Dissolving the Pain-Body
279wajietongkuzhishen.excerpt: By Eckhart Tolle; translated by Zhang Defen.

280kuoranwusheng.title: Vast Emptiness, No Sage
280kuoranwusheng.author: Zhiyu
280kuoranwusheng.excerpt: Emperor Wu of Liang asked Great Master Bodhidharma: “What is the foremost meaning of the holy truth?” Bodhidharma said: “Vast emptiness, no sage!” The Emperor said: “Who, then, is facing me?” Bodhidharma said: “I don’t know.” The Emperor did not awaken, and Bodhidharma thereupon crossed the river to Wei.

281yinianbusheng.title: Not a Single Thought Arises, Yet All Is Distinctly Clear
281yinianbusheng.author: Zhanran
281yinianbusheng.excerpt: Question: Is "not a single thought arising, yet all distinctly clear" a good state or a bad state? Why do some Chan masters scold this state so severely?

282qishianxin.title: Begging the Master to Pacify the Mind
282qishianxin.author: Annotated by Zhiyu
282qishianxin.excerpt: On the night of the ninth day of the twelfth month of that year, a great snow fell. Guang stood firm and unmoving, and by dawn the snow had piled past his knees. The Patriarch, taking pity, asked: “You have stood long in the snow—what is it you seek?” Guang answered with tears: “I only wish that the Master, in his compassion, would open the gate of sweet dew and broadly deliver the host of beings.” The Patriarch said: “The unsurpassed wondrous Way of the Buddhas requires diligent effort across kalpas without end—doing what is hard to do, enduring what cannot be endured.”

283kongjudeyuantou.title: The Source of Fear
283kongjudeyuantou.excerpt: By Eckhart Tolle; translated by Zhang Defen

284erzhonggenben.title: The Two Fundamental Roots
284erzhonggenben.author: Annotated by Zhiyu
284erzhonggenben.excerpt: [All sentient beings, from the beginningless eon, birth and death following in unbroken succession, are all because they do not know the abiding true mind, the pure, bright substance of its nature, but put to use all their delusive thoughts; and because these thoughts are not true, there is the wheel of turning.]

285jingzhongjie.title: The Admonishing Verse of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva
285jingzhongjie.excerpt: Time passes swiftly, and human life is impermanent. Those who study the Buddha-Dharma must remain ever vigilant, and must never be careless, frolic in idle pleasures, or squander their time and end in endless regret.

291xiuxingdezhendi.title: The True Meaning of Practice
291xiuxingdezhendi.excerpt: The mind is like a continuously flowing river. If you cannot use your practice to grasp it in every present moment, then the mantras you recite, the visualizations you do, the chanting, the meditation, and even the lofty views you express and the exalted conduct you display — all of this is merely wasting time.

292wuzhongzuiqiangdadeliliang.title: The Five Mightiest Powers
292wuzhongzuiqiangdadeliliang.author: The Essence of Practice
292wuzhongzuiqiangdadeliliang.excerpt: For practice to become a way of life, one should cultivate the five powers. If we possess these five powers, bodhicitta will naturally arise in the mind.

301jgj.excerpt: All that has marks is false and deceptive; take not hold of marks, and abide unmoved in suchness.

302xinj.title: The Heart Sutra Explained
302xinj.excerpt: The Buddha taught and expounded the Dharma for forty-nine years, and of those years twenty-two were given to the prajñā scriptures. It may be said that the prajñā scriptures are the soul of the whole Dharma, that the Diamond Sutra is the essence of the prajñā scriptures, and that the Heart Sutra is in turn the essence of the Diamond Sutra. That is why, for a thousand years, the Heart Sutra has been known to every household and on every lip.

303liuzutanjing.author: Annotated by Zhanran
303liuzutanjing.excerpt: The Platform Sutra is the only work of indigenous Chinese Buddhism honored with the title of a sutra. Its appearance marks the formal establishment of Chinese Chan Buddhism, and it shines with boundless light.

304fozangj.title: Selected Annotations on the Buddha-Treasure Sūtra
304fozangj.author: Zhanran, selected and annotated
304fozangj.excerpt: The Buddha-Treasure Sūtra, in three fascicles. The whole sūtra is divided into ten chapters, discussing the reality of all dharmas as non-arising and non-ceasing, without characteristics and without activity. 402nianfolun.title: On Buddha-Recitation (Annotated Sayings of Master Chewu)
402nianfolun.author: Compiled and annotated by Zhanran
402nianfolun.excerpt: A single recitation of the Buddha’s name, free of all other conditions; when the ten recitations are perfected, one instantly transcends many kalpas.

403chanjing.title: The Essentials of Chan and Pure Land (Annotated from Master Hanshan's Record of Instructions)
403chanjing.author: Compiled and annotated by Zhanran
403chanjing.excerpt: Surveying the whole course of Master Hanshan's life, we see that, like Master Yongming (the Sixth Patriarch of the Pure Land school) and Master Chewu (the Twelfth Patriarch of the Pure Land school), his cultivation and his propagation of both Chan and Pure Land were outstanding and shining, and his name is recorded in the Record of Sages of the Pure Land; thus he is both a Chan-lineage master and a Pure Land-lineage master. Only because

404nianfosanmei.title: A Detailed Explanation of “Record of Groping for the Elephant in Buddha-Recitation-Samādhi”
404nianfosanmei.author: Annotated by Zhanran
404nianfosanmei.excerpt: The essay “Record of Groping for the Elephant in Buddha-Recitation-Samādhi” is preserved in Master Yinguang’s Collected Writings, Volume Four. It is the original manuscript of Master Liaoyu, revised by Master Yinguang before publication, and therefore embodies Master Yinguang’s own experience and insight in cultivating Buddha-recitation-samādhi as well. It is a rare and precious document within the practice of Buddha-recitation. It sets forth in depth the method, the stages, the marks, the function, the essence, and the benefits of Buddha-recitation-samādhi, and in its latter half explains how, once Buddha-recitation-samādhi has been attained, one should carry on the work of preserving the realization.

502xiuxinjue.title: A Detailed Explanation of the Essentials of Mind Cultivation
502xiuxinjue.excerpt: Composed by State Preceptor Bojo Jinul of Goryeo. Annotated by Zhanran.

502yuanjuejingjj.title: A Precise Explanation of the Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment
502yuanjuejingjj.author: Annotated by Zhanran
502yuanjuejingjj.excerpt: The full title of the Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment is The Great, Vast Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment, the Sutra of Definitive Meaning. It has twelve chapters. In it Śākyamuni Buddha, through dialogues with twelve great bodhisattvas, proclaims the wondrous principle of the Tathagata's perfect enlightenment (the perfect enlightenment of the self-nature) and the methods of cultivation.
